Shadow mode duplicates requests to a new model without using its decisions, revealing latency and output differences but not user-response effects. Canary deployment serves a small real-traffic fraction and expands when guardrails pass. Blue-green maintains two complete environments and switches traffic, making rollback straightforward if dependencies are compatible. [1](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

Bandit allocation adaptively favors actions with better observed reward while exploring others. It can reduce opportunity cost, but complicates inference and may starve slower or delayed-reward variants. [4](https://incompleteideas.net/book/the-book-2nd.html)

Choose according to risk and objective. All need versioned artifacts, monitoring, explicit promotion criteria, and rollback. Shadows must not duplicate external side effects. A canary without randomized comparison can confound model effects with traffic composition; infrastructure safety and causal product evaluation are separate checks.
